reason: Batch of independently reviewed PRs, each green on its own: #1023: Rolling Core releases. serve adopts an inherited listening socket (LISTEN_FDS or --listen-fd), validated before ownership and detached on failure, and probes with SO_REUSEADDR. While a holder keeps the socket, a stopping supervisor closes only relayed exchanges that already answered (after 5 s) and never one awaiting its receipt (up to 30 s); after that, connections whose client stopped reading get a 5 s flush and are aborted, with a 50 s uvicorn backstop; a self-bound listener relays to completion. Deployment operations run shielded, answer 503 with their operation ID and Retry-After if their request is cancelled (the deployer's deployment_post and the rehearsal roll honour it), and are joined before host authority is released. Workers resend read-only host observations only while the host is being replaced (connect failure or the undispatched 503); peer capacity and peer failures fail at once; queued host-pressure callers share one observation. The handoff inventory keeps a project finishing while a queued follow-up dispatch is in flight. Selected suites cover the deployer's operation client, the handoff agent, listener adoption and drain, the management ledger, IPC, host-service replacement and resend bounds, supervisor lifecycle and bootstrap, the browser bridge and the remote host-pressure gate. #1021: Three shutdown hangs and one log flood. (1) After any supervisor restart, verified handoff/recovery rows whose target no longer owns the project were re-advanced every 0.5 s, failing LeaseLost and logging runtime.project_restore.waiting at ERROR forever; the loop now selects verified rows only while their target still owns the project, logs a waiting transfer once per reason, and writes blockers only when they change. (2) SIGTERM or a confirmed shutdown waited without limit for open viewer streams relayed from workers; the stable listener now has a 5 s graceful shutdown bound. (3) A cancellation swallowed below a loop (Python 3.11 wait_for in the SQLAlchemy pool, or a driver error during cancel cleanup) left storage dispatch and chat follow-ups running after their single cancel(); they now stop on a flag and are re-cancelled until done; inside #1024's event-driven follow-up loop the flag is checked before each step and after each pass, and shutdown also wakes the waiter. Selected tests cover each mechanism directly. #1048: Owner decision: a queued follow-up parks for review only when a security-relevant runtime field changes. The queue compared the provider/harness profile revision, and every harness turn records session/turn evidence on its profile, so a follow-up queued during a harness turn always parked with 'Runtime authorization changed'. The queue now stores and compares a digest of the profile's authorization fields (harness: kind, connection, executable/home/endpoint, auth and secret ref, default model, permission mode, privacy, native capabilities; provider: type, endpoint, locality, secret refs, model allowlist/default model, capabilities, privacy, per-model verification status); legacy items keep the revision comparison. test_reviewed_follow_up_releases_completed_harness_goal_handoff now parks via a permission change (deliberate contract change). Selected: the harness goal/queue suite with the new both-way tests, the chat queue suite and queue positions. #1055: SQL-global mutations (project create, provider/harness/MCP profile CRUD, global settings) commit in GlobalSqlDelivery.execute before the API worker responds, but that branch called response_view without the receipt, so with every control viewer busy a saved project came back as 429 'Viewer capacity is busy; reconnect using the saved request ID' with no ID; clients that resubmitted with a new Idempotency-Key created duplicates. The branch now passes its receipt like the project-command and work-batch branches (202 + X-Nebula-Command-Id; following it returns the saved 201). Selected: the global API suite (new regression test), API worker and composition, global settings and work suites. #1056: ModelBroker returned Application Model refusals (stale revision, schema-invalid relationship/type/property, unknown object) as exit_code 1 output without a receipt, so the provider chat loop rebuilt the failure from a generic RuntimeError and the model saw only 'The tool could not complete.' with unknown side effects. ModelBroker now attaches a GuidedToolError as failure_error (the MCP path's mechanism): Core's fixed refusal sentence or the fixed prefix of an interpolated one (never argument values or graph content), 'Nothing was saved', and next steps naming model.relationship_options / model.discover_schema / the current revision. Direct callers keep the output and recovery. The COMPLETE ledger transition moved out of the refusal handler. Selected: Application Model API/broker suites (with the new chat-level regression test), execution-scope and admission suites for the model tools, and the shared tool failure guidance suite. #1051: #939 made BrowserAutomationService.create_lease/revoke_run and RuntimePlatform.chat_components coroutines, but MissionService.start_mission, MissionService._revoke_browser_control and AutomationToolPlatform.mission_components kept calling them without await. Native browser-autonomy missions were queued with no browser lease (and a refused lease was accepted as 202), stopped/failed/finished missions never revoked their lease, and every native mission with an MCP server failed preflight with "'coroutine' object has no attribute 'specs'". The fix awaits all three and makes _revoke_browser_control async at its five callers. Selected: the new route-level regressions (browser lease created, lease refusal fails the run with 422, stop and failure revoke the lease and free the session, MCP mission starts with and without browser autonomy) plus the repaired browser-mission test; every test_missions case that passes on origin/main (start/stop/startup reconcile/recovery paths that now await revocation); the browser automation service suite; mission checkpoint retention cases that pass on main; and the browser and automation mission_components output-budget cases. #1059: Two harness-gateway coroutines left un-awaited by #939. (1) harness_core_tools.call_core_tool's SubagentWaitPending branch called the now-async _invoking_child, wait_ready and wait_result without await, so a harness subagent's message_parent(wait_for_reply) failed at once instead of waiting for the parent's answer. (2) PermissionTicket.acknowledge_handoff called the async record_adapter_handoff without await, so every Codex/Grok/Claude SDK approval kept adapter_status 'pending'. Awaiting the receipt exposed a revision race between the decision task's record_delivery and the adapter's receipt on the same approval; both now reread and replan after a revision conflict. Selected: the approval handoff suite (new real-consumer, product-ticket and race tests plus the 4 contract tests that were red on main), the adapter and Codex transport suites that build permission tickets, the passing approval-continuation delivery tests, the harness subagent suite repaired in this change (new gateway question test) minus three load-sensitive cases, and the Grok/Codex permission-answer and harness approval-policy cases. #1046: tests/v3/application_model_fixture.py, the Core behind the working-knowledge, assistant-browser-viewer, project-deletion and workspace-quota Playwright areas, still called NebulaStore.create, the async SQLAlchemy engine and store.get/create in its unused-harness-session route synchronously after #939 made Core storage async. It crashed with AttributeError: 'coroutine' object has no attribute 'id' before uvicorn started, so all four areas failed at webServer startup on main. The fixture now runs its seeding, the legacy-graph insert and uvicorn.Server.serve() inside one asyncio.run(main()), and the fixture route is async. Selected: every catalogued case of working-knowledge, project-deletion and workspace-quota (8 projects each). working-knowledge also needs the Application Model API fix from #1015, already on main. #1047: Host pressure thresholds were capped at 100% while CPU use reads 100% and runnable tasks per CPU exceed 1 on a saturated host, so no setting could admit a new start. A threshold of 100% now turns its check off; Settings shows it as Off; operator help, settings search, settings assistant guidance and destinations explain it; the terminal keeps Core's queue reason beside the position. Selected: host-pressure evaluation, live settings and settings-assistant use (new off and saturated-host tests), host-load gate, product help discovery (new test), the terminal shell (new queue-reason test), the host pressure settings component and catalog discovery tests, and the host-load admission Playwright journey.
exclusions: #1023: Per-test selections exclude cases that fail identically on clean main: the product-guidance mirror and API-peer 401/404 cases in test_runtime_host_services.py, test_owned_project_refuses_real_shutdown_without_notifying_launcher in test_runtime_management.py (expects 'uncertain'; #1019 makes it 'failed'), test_shared_automation_image_prepare_replay_and_changed_runner in test_runtime_host_observations.py, and test_staged_deployer.py (its test_lost_handoff_reply_reconciles_before_retiring_or_advancing fails on main). Process-level suites need a pidfd-capable Python with Nebula importable by spawned workers; locally they ran on Python 3.12 (SQLite as in CI; earlier also PostgreSQL). Under heavy shared-host load the existing 20 s worker readiness bound can time out spawn-based tests; reruns pass. No UI, native or Playwright cases: no frontend code changed; browser reconnect across a host swap is recorded as unverified. scripts/deploy_rehearsal and the docs are rehearsal tooling and evidence (E1-E7c in docs/validation/rolling-core-releases.md), not run by CI. #1021: No UI, native or Playwright cases: no frontend code changed. test_recovery_reconciliation.py spawns real processes; it was run with a per-worktree Python 3.12 venv (nebula resolving to this worktree) and passes in full, as on main. test_runtime_processes.py has 4 failures that are identical on main 936b5d5 (from #1022's StartAborted; fixed separately), so it is not selected. PostgreSQL variants run where NEBULA_TEST_POSTGRES_URL is set. Real-Core evidence (SIGTERM with an open /api/v1/work/events stream: >90 s on main, 5.5 s here; restore-waiting flood: ~320/min on main, 0 here on the same database) is in the PR body. #1048: test_harness_chat_goals.py::test_late_subagent_report_resumes_parked_harness_goal_once (flaky on main; fixed separately in #1026) and ::test_goal_resume_uses_saved_next_harness_in_same_chat (2 params) fail identically on pristine origin/main and with this patch, so they are excluded. No UI, native or Playwright cases: no frontend code changed. No real-Core check: this host has no inert harness executable (the installed vendor CLIs would contact external services). #1055: No UI, native or Playwright cases: no frontend code changed; the UI already follows 202 receipts. Real-Core evidence (scratch Postgres Core with all control viewers held: 202 receipt, followed 201, same-key retry returns the same project, one project) is recorded in the PR, not executed by CI. #1056: test_all_tool_failure_guidance.py::test_security_read_refusal_names_session_prerequisite and ::test_gateway_preserves_guided_error_and_actual_offered_usage fail identically on pristine origin/main and with this patch, so they are excluded. No UI, native or Playwright cases: no frontend code changed. The harness MCP gateway path is unchanged (it already exposes the full output through a tool_output.read artifact). No real-Core check: the host-pressure gate held every chat turn while host CPU stayed at 100%; see the PR. #1051: No full suites. No frontend, native or Playwright changes; the fix is Core-only and was exercised through the same /api/v1/missions, /runs/{id}/stop and /runs/{id}/browser-automation endpoints the Workbench Browser, New Mission dialog and Butler use on a scratch supervisor Core (evidence in the PR body). The real-Core Playwright area butler-browser-mission asserts this lease but is not selected: it fails on origin/main by construction and was not run locally under the shared host load. Other cases in tests/v3/test_missions.py (9), test_automation_runtime.py (7), test_mission_checkpoint_retention.py (2), test_model_output_budget.py (9), test_control_assistant_work.py (36) and test_chat_subagents.py (22) fail identically on pristine origin/main (unawaited test-client and fixture calls left by the async conversion), so they cannot prove this change; the branch adds no new failures in any of those files. #1059: No full suites; no frontend, native or Playwright changes (Core-only fix, no UI). Excluded because they fail identically on pristine origin/main for reasons this change does not touch: test_approval_continuation.py::test_cancelled_waiter_does_not_resurrect_terminal_turn and ::test_resolving_one_request_keeps_the_other_pending; 5 test_grok_acp_compliance, 4 test_harness_leftovers, 1 test_codex_turn_outcomes, 4 test_subagent_refusal_categories, 17 test_universal_agent_tools and 22 test_chat_subagents cases (identical failure sets on main and branch); test_harnesses.py::test_late_approval_decision_does_not_break_the_gateway and ::test_harness_api_chat_mission_handoff_and_catalog (same assertion failures on main). test_harness_provider_subagents.py was inert on main (un-awaited prepare_chat); of its repaired cases, test_harness_subagent_stop_cancels_its_harness_turn, test_harness_mission_supervisor_uses_chat_gateway_and_records_child and test_operator_limit_reaches_the_harness_and_is_enforced hit pre-existing load-dependent races (subagent.stop revision conflict, 5 s waits, prepare_chat session revision conflict) with or without this fix, so they are not selected. test_terminal_core.py is only updated to the async receipt contract; its approval case fails on main for unrelated reasons. Other suites importing _prepare (subagent_delivery, mcp_catalog_reads, subagent_start_replay, universal_agent_tools, subagent_refusal_categories) still call it without await, exactly as on main; not repaired here. No live provider or harness accounts and no Core deployment. #1046: area:assistant-browser-viewer is left out although this fixture serves it: with the fixture repaired it fails intermittently (CI run 43617668265 on model-compact and model-webkit-320; locally on WebKit) at spec line 53 because PUT /api/v1/browser-companion/{id}/control?paused=false returns 409 'revision conflict: expected 4, found 5'. BrowserCompanionService.takeover reads the BrowserSession and updates it with expected_revision while the viewer's 3-second tabs poll (request() rewrites the same row) and the reconnect open() also write it; the UI only logs the failure, so the Resume control silently stays paused. That is a product race reported separately, not a fixture or spec fault. No Python, frontend or native tests: only a Playwright fixture under tests/v3 changed; no product, UI or API code changed. Other Playwright fixtures broken by #939 (thinking, workspace_recovery, host_mode, host_cpu_budget, universal_agent) are repaired in a separate PR. #1047: test_product_knowledge::test_product_search_finds_headless_core_and_paired_butler_cli fails identically on pristine origin/main (22b46bf, freshly built index) and is not selected. No native change. The host-load admission Playwright area runs in CI. Its model-webkit-430 run failed on the spec's first send because of a pre-existing composer draft race (text typed before the conversation's draft storage scope loads moves to the earlier draft key, assigned separately); the spec now retypes until Send takes the request, and passed 3 of 3 locally on model-webkit-430 against the production bundle and the real host-load fixture.
